header.title: Account
header.description: Your profile, preferences, sign-in methods and activity.

profile.securityProtected: Protected with MFA: a passkey, two-step verification or a connected account with two-factor authentication. Your password and connected accounts are on the Security page too.
profile.securityUnprotected: Add a passkey or two-step verification so a stolen password isn't enough to get in. Your password and connected accounts are on the Security page.
profile.emailVerifiedDescription: The address you sign in with and get emails on.
profile.emailUnverifiedDescription: The address you sign in with and get emails on. Verify it, so we know it reaches you.
profile.nameDescription: How you're shown to others in Adiutor.
profile.activityEmpty: Sign-ins and changes to your account will show up here.
profile.activityDescription: Sign-ins and changes to your account, newest first. Don't recognise something? Change your password and sign out your other devices.
profile.pictureDescription: Shown next to your name wherever people see it in Adiutor. It comes from an account you connected; Adiutor stores no files.
profile.pictureNotYet: Sign in with {provider} once to use its picture.
profile.pictureDefault: {shown, select, initials {Until you choose, your initials are shown.} other {Until you choose, the picture of the account you connected first is shown.}}
profile.pictureConnect: Connect GitHub or Google on the <link>Security page</link> to use its picture.
profile.alreadyVerified: Your email address is already verified.
profile.verificationFailed: Sending the email failed. Please try again.
profile.verificationSent: We've sent a verification link to {email}. It expires in 1 hour.
profile.languageDescription: Adiutor and the emails it sends you use this language.
profile.languageNotOffered: You chose {language}, which isn't offered right now, so Adiutor uses the default language until it is.
profile.timeZoneDescription: Adiutor shows times in this zone on every device you sign in on, and in the emails it sends you.
profile.requestEmailsDescription: An email when someone replies to a request you’re on or changes its status, and when someone puts you on one. Unsubscribing from a request stops its emails; turning these off stops all of them, also for requests assigned to you.

messages.verificationExpired: This verification link has expired. Send a new one.
messages.verificationInvalid: This verification link is invalid. Send a new one.
messages.emailNotVerified: The provider hasn't verified that account's email address.
messages.failed: That didn’t work. Please try again.
messages.disconnectNotFresh: For your safety, sign out and in again before disconnecting.
messages.disconnectMfaRequired: Your role requires MFA, and this account gives you it. Add a passkey first, then try again.

security.title: Security
security.mustSetUp: {emailCodes, select, true {Your role requires MFA. Add a passkey or set up an authenticator app to continue using Adiutor. Email codes aren’t enough for your role.} other {Your role requires MFA. Add a passkey or set up an authenticator app to continue using Adiutor.}}
security.recommended: Recommended: add a passkey or turn on two-step verification, so a stolen password isn't enough to get into your account.
security.keepLastPasskey: Your role requires MFA, so keep this passkey until you've added another passkey or an authenticator app.
security.keepAuthenticator: Your role requires MFA, so your authenticator app stays on. To move it to a new phone, add a passkey first, then turn this off and set it up again.
security.keepMfaProvider: Your role requires MFA, and your {providers} account with two-factor authentication gives you it. Add a passkey or an authenticator app before disconnecting it.
security.providerMfaOnly: Your role requires MFA, and {providers} with two-factor authentication only counts while you have no password and every connected account has it. Add a passkey or an authenticator app first.
security.currentPasswordHint: To keep your account safe, confirm it's you.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of a password. A passkey can't be phished and counts as two-step protection on its own.
passkeys.removeDescription: You won't be able to sign in with this passkey anymore. Also remove it from your device or password manager.
passkeys.created: {name} was added. You can now sign in with it.
passkeys.addDescription: Give it a name, then follow your browser's prompt.
passkeys.nameHint: So you can tell your passkeys apart, e.g. “Work laptop” or “iPhone”.

twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
twoFactor.description: After your password, enter a code from an authenticator app or from an email. You also confirm with it after signing in with an email link, or with a connected account that can't prove two-factor authentication.
twoFactor.turnOffNote: Turning it off makes your password enough to sign in.
twoFactor.emailReplaced: Your authenticator app replaces them, so your inbox alone can’t get in.
twoFactor.emailNotForRole: They don’t count for your role. Set up an authenticator app or add a passkey.
twoFactor.authenticatorSetUp: Set up, with backup codes for when you lose your phone.
twoFactor.authenticatorNotSetUp: Codes that work offline, plus backup codes.
twoFactor.backupDescription: Your current backup codes stop working.
twoFactor.turnOffDescription: Your password alone will be enough to sign in. Your authenticator app and backup codes stop working.

backupCodes.intro: Use one of these if you can't use your authenticator app. Each works once. Keep them somewhere safe, like a password manager: they won't be shown again.
backupCodes.label: Backup codes

authenticator.title: Set up an authenticator app
authenticator.description: Use an app like 1Password, Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator.
authenticator.backupDescription: Your authenticator app is set up.
authenticator.scan: Scan this QR code with your app.
authenticator.qrAlt: QR code to add Adiutor to your authenticator app
authenticator.manualKey: Can't scan it? Enter this key instead: {key}
authenticator.enterCode: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows.

emailCodes.title: Use email codes
emailCodes.description: After your password, you'll enter a code we email to {email}.
emailCodes.send: Send a code to check it works
emailCodes.sent: {minutes, plural, one {We sent a code to {email}. It expires in # minute.} other {We sent a code to {email}. It expires in # minutes.}}
emailCodes.sentAgain: {minutes, plural, one {We sent a new code to {email}. It expires in # minute.} other {We sent a new code to {email}. It expires in # minutes.}}

connected.title: Connected accounts
connected.description: {count, plural, one {Connect {providers} to sign in with it. The account's email may differ from yours.} other {Connect {providers} to sign in with them. The account's email may differ from yours.}}
connected.unconfirmedMfa: Connected {date} when you signed in with it. Confirm it to use it as your second step, or disconnect it if it isn't yours.
connected.unconfirmed: Connected {date} when you signed in with it. Confirm it if it's yours, or disconnect it if it isn't yours.
connected.disconnectDescription: You can't sign in with this {provider} account until you connect it again.
connected.noLongerConnected: That account is no longer connected.

password.title: Password
password.descriptionChange: Changing it signs you out on your other devices.
password.descriptionSet: You don't have a password yet; you sign in with an email link or another provider. Set one to also sign in with your email and password.
password.failed: Saving the password failed. Please try again.

sessions.title: Signed-in devices
sessions.description: Browsers where you're signed in. If you don't recognise one, sign it out and change your password. Signing out a device also makes every browser you trusted ask for your code again, this one included.
sessions.caption: Your signed-in devices
sessions.signOutOthersTitle: Sign out on all other devices?
sessions.signOutOthersDescription: You stay signed in here. Everywhere else you'll have to sign in again, and browsers you trusted, this one included, will ask for your code again.
sessions.signedOutOthers: {count, plural, one {Signed out on # other device.} other {Signed out on # other devices.}}

deactivate.title: Deactivate account
deactivate.description: You're signed out everywhere and can't sign in until an Admin reactivates your account. Nothing is deleted.
deactivate.dialogDescription: You're signed out on every device right away. To use Adiutor again, ask an Admin to reactivate your account.

staffSignIn.title: Sign-ins by staff
staffSignIn.description: {minutes, plural, one {Adiutor staff can sign in as you for up to # minute, to see what you see and check what isn't working for you. They can work on your requests, and you'll see it was them; they can't change anything else. You get an email each time.} other {Adiutor staff can sign in as you for up to # minutes, to see what you see and check what isn't working for you. They can work on your requests, and you'll see it was them; they can't change anything else. You get an email each time.}}

signedInAs.note: You're viewing {name}'s account pages as they see them. Nothing can be changed here while you're signed in as them.
signedInAs.leftOut: Some of their personal details are left out, as on <link>their user page</link>.
signedInAs.mustSetUpMfa: {name} has to set up MFA before they can use Adiutor, so this Security page is what they see now.
